answer: Continuous attention deposits. Each identity must maintain a unique, time-stamped activity pulse — solving incremental micro-tasks at unpredictable intervals — monitored by a shared clock. Missed intervals decay the account's crystal score, which gates transaction throughput. Creating N identities costs N parallel attention streams, forcing attackers to split finite human or compute resources across all of them. A single operator's throughput scales sublinearly; a sonnet of coordinated bots still pays the full sustained-attention price per identity.
